title: Go: database/sql Patterns
description: Master Go's database/sql package with connection management, prepared statements, transactions, and error handling.

steps.title: Open a database connection
steps.description: Use `sql.Open` to connect to a SQLite database (simulated, use `:memory:`). Call `.Ping()` to verify connectivity. Configure `SetMaxOpenConns(10)` and `SetMaxIdleConns(5)`. Print connection info using `fmt.Printf`.
hints: Import _ "modernc.org/sqlite" or use a simulated driver

steps.title: Query and scan rows
steps.description: Execute `SELECT * FROM users` using `db.QueryContext(ctx, query)` and iterate with `rows.Next()`. Use `rows.Scan(&id, &name, &email)` to destructure each row. Print each user using `fmt.Printf("User: %d, %s, %s\n", ...)`.

verification.failureMessage: Print each user as 'User: id, name, email'.

steps.title: Prepared statements
steps.description: Use `db.PrepareContext(ctx, "INSERT INTO users(name, email) VALUES($1, $2)")` to create a prepared statement. Execute it multiple times with different parameters using `stmt.ExecContext(ctx, name, email)`. Print inserted IDs using `fmt.Printf`.
hints: Prepared statement is safe from SQL injection

verification.failureMessage: Print the IDs of inserted rows.

steps.title: Transactions with Commit and Rollback
steps.description: Start a transaction with `db.BeginTx(ctx, nil)`. Insert two users, then intentionally cause an error on the third insert. Call `tx.Rollback()`. Then start a new transaction that succeeds and call `tx.Commit()`. Print transaction status using `fmt.Println`.
hints: Use defer tx.Rollback() even after successful commits (safe no-op)
Return error to trigger rollback path
Print 'committed' or 'rolled back' for each transaction

verification.failureMessage: Print the result of each transaction.

steps.title: Error handling patterns
steps.description: Demonstrate Go database error handling: check for `sql.ErrNoRows` when `QueryRow.Scan` returns no results, handle constraint violations (unique constraint), and use `errors.Is` for error comparison. Print each error type using `fmt.Printf`.
hints: QueryRow.Scan returns sql.ErrNoRows on empty result
Constraint violations are driver-specific but implement error interface

verification.failureMessage: Print each type of database error encountered.

steps.title: Connection pooling stats
steps.description: Call `db.Stats()` to get `sql.DBStats` and print connection pool statistics: open connections, in-use, idle, wait count, wait duration (use `fmt.Printf`). Simulate concurrent queries with goroutines and `sync.WaitGroup`.
hints: DBStats has OpenConnections, InUse, Idle fields
Stats() returns a snapshot, call it before and after
Use a WaitGroup to coordinate goroutines

verification.failureMessage: Print Open, InUse, and Idle connection counts.
